subproblem.title: Local masses of a current in ℝ^P versus its restriction to U and versus a current in U agreeing with it near G (the parent's (p4) and step 8(c))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n). For a current D in a domain V, M_G(D) = D.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(D(ω)) over all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x (SimonGMT massAdmissibleOn). Then: (a) M_G(X|_U) ≤ M_G(X), where X|_U := X.restrictDomain(U ⊆ ℝ^P), X|_U(ω) = X(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); (b) if G ⊆ U and X(ω) = Z(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G (on the left, ω is regarded as a test form on ℝ^P via testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U)), then M_G(X) ≤ M_G(Z).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (X.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).massOn G ≤ X.massOn G ∧ (G ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → X (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω) = Z ω) → X.massOn G ≤ Z.massOn G)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: (p4) of the parent proof (M_G(X|_U) ≤ M_G(X): a form admissible for M_G(X|_U) is admissible for M_G(X), with the same value) and step 8(c) (a form admissible for M_{B_G}(QY) is admissible for M_{B_G}(Z), and QY agrees with Z on it), stated for arbitrary X, Z, U and G.
Call ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) admissible for M_G in the domain V if tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ι(ω) ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) denotes the same form regarded on ℝ^P (testFormOnInclusion); its topological support and its pointwise values are those of ω.
1. (Proof of (a).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) be admissible for M_G in U. Then ι(ω) is admissible for M_G in ℝ^P (same support and same pointwise norms), and X|_U(ω) = X(ι(ω)) by the definition of restrictDomain. So ofReal(X|_U(ω)) = ofReal(X(ι(ω))) ≤ M_G(X). Taking the supremum over all such ω gives M_G(X|_U) ≤ M_G(X).
2. (Proof of (b).) Assume G ⊆ U and the agreement hypothesis, and let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be admissible for M_G in ℝ^P. The underlying form of ω is smooth with compact support, and tsupport ω ⊆ G ⊆ U, so it defines an element ω′ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ι(ω′) = ω (same underlying form). ω′ is admissible for M_G in U (tsupport ω′ = tsupport ω ⊆ G, same pointwise norms), and by hypothesis X(ω) = X(ι(ω′)) = Z(ω′). Hence ofReal(X(ω)) = ofReal(Z(ω′)) ≤ M_G(Z). Taking the supremum over all such ω gives M_G(X) ≤ M_G(Z). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a): an admissible ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) gives the admissible ι(ω) ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with X|_U(ω) = X(ι(ω)); take the supremum.
(b): an admissible ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ G ⊆ U equals ι(ω′) for an admissible ω′ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and X(ω) = Z(ω′); take the supremum.

audit.reason: Both inequalities follow by transporting admissible test forms with unchanged evaluations and norms. The reverse transport uses precisely G ⊆ U. The proof works for arbitrary U and G and requires no undeclared dependency.

subproblem.title: Minimality against adding an integer multiplicity cycle supported in A ∩ W (step 5 of the parent)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, A ⊆ ℝ^P, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in A (contract IsMinimizingIn T A: T is integer multiplicity and M_{W′}(T) ≤ M_{W′}(S) for every open W′ ⊂⊂ U and every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with ∂S = ∂T and spt(S − T) a compact subset of A ∩ W′). Let W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with W ⊂⊂ U (contract CompactlyContained W U: closure(W) is compact and contained in U). Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) be integer multiplicity with ∂X = 0, spt X compact and spt X ⊆ A ∩ W, and let Z₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy Z₁(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where X is evaluated at ω regarded as a test form on ℝ^P (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U)). Then M_W(T) ≤ M_W(Z₁) (SimonGMT massOn).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U A W : Set (Euclid P)) (T Z₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn T A → IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → X.boundary = 0 → IsCompact X.support → X.support ⊆ A ∩ W → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), Z₁ ω = T ω + X (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) (m + 1) ω)) → T.massOn W ≤ Z₁.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (the competitor Z₁ = T + (push Y)|_U: (i) same boundary, (ii)–(iii) compact support of Z₁ − T in A ∩ B_{G₃}, (iv) B_{G₃} ⊂⊂ U, and minimality), with the cycle push Y replaced by an arbitrary X and B_{G₃} by W. Simon 7.1.1 and 7.2.4 with Remark 7.2.5(2). Siblings: (IMC) im_calculus, part (c); (RO) restrict_open_im.
Notation. For D ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), D|_U := D.restrictDomain(U ⊆ ℝ^P) ∈ 𝒟_k(U), so D|_U(ω) = D(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), regarded in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with the same underlying form. For a current D in a domain V, spt D = V ∖ Z_D, where Z_D is the union of the open sets W′ with compact closure contained in V on which D vanishes; Z_D is open. Currents are determined by their values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
1. (Z₁ is integer multiplicity.) T is integer multiplicity (first part of IsMinimizingIn T A). X|_U is integer multiplicity by (RO), U being open. By (IMC)(c) in U, N := X|_U − X|_U, then N − X|_U, then T − (N − X|_U) are integer multiplicity. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): (T − (N − X|_U))(ω) = T(ω) − (0 − X(ω)) = T(ω) + X(ω) = Z₁(ω). Hence Z₁ = T − (N − X|_U) is integer multiplicity.
2. (∂Z₁ = ∂T.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). The form dη ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), regarded in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), is the exterior derivative of η regarded in 𝒟^m(ℝ^P): both have underlying form dη (exteriorDerivativeTestOn does not depend on the domain). Hence ∂Z₁(η) = Z₁(dη) = T(dη) + X(dη) = ∂T(η) + ∂X(η) = ∂T(η), because ∂X = 0. So ∂Z₁ = ∂T, which is SameBoundary Z₁ T in degree n = m + 1.
3. (spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt X.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), (Z₁ − T)(ω) = Z₁(ω) − T(ω) = X(ω). Let x ∈ spt(Z₁ − T); then x ∈ U. Suppose x ∉ spt X. Then x ∈ Z_X: there is an open V ∋ x on which X vanishes. As U is open, choose r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U and put V′ := V ∩ B_{r/2}(x). V′ is open and contains x; closure(V′) ⊆ closedBall(x, r/2) ⊆ B_r(x) ⊆ U, and closure(V′) is compact (a closed subset of the compact closedBall(x, r/2)). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V′ ⊆ V: (Z₁ − T)(ω) = X(ω) = 0. So Z₁ − T vanishes on V′ and x ∈ Z_{Z₁−T}, contradicting x ∈ spt(Z₁ − T). Hence spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt X ⊆ A ∩ W.
4. (Compactness.) spt X ⊆ W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ U. Therefore spt(Z₁ − T) = U ∖ Z_{Z₁−T} equals spt X ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ Z_{Z₁−T}): '⊆' by step 3, and '⊇' because every point of spt X lies in U. This is the intersection of the compact set spt X with a closed set, hence compact.
5. (Minimality.) W is open with W ⊂⊂ U, Z₁ is integer multiplicity (step 1), SameBoundary Z₁ T (step 2), and spt(Z₁ − T) is compact (step 4) and contained in A ∩ W (step 3). The second part of IsMinimizingIn T A, applied to W and S := Z₁, gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(Z₁). ∎
proof_key_steps: Z₁ = T − ((X|_U − X|_U) − X|_U) is integer multiplicity by (RO) and (IMC)(c).
∂Z₁(η) = T(dη) + X(dη) = ∂T(η) because ∂X = 0; so SameBoundary Z₁ T.
(Z₁ − T)(ω) = X(ω); a point of U outside spt X has a small open neighbourhood with compact closure in U on which Z₁ − T vanishes, so spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt X ⊆ A ∩ W.
spt(Z₁ − T) = spt X ∖ Z_{Z₁−T} is compact; minimality with W and S = Z₁ gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(Z₁).

audit.reason: The proof verifies integer multiplicity, boundary equality, support containment and compactness before invoking the exact minimizing contract. Derivative inclusion commutes definitionally, and CompactlyContained W U ensures the compact ambient support lies in U.

subproblem.title: Subadditivity of the mass measures of integer multiplicity currents on closed sets (step 8(b) of the parent)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, X, X₁, X₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n), and R, R₁, R₂ IMReps in V (contract IMRep V n) with R representing X, R₁ representing X₁ and R₂ representing X₂. Suppose X(ω) = X₁(ω) + X₂(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). Then for every closed set F ⊆ ℝ^P with F ⊆ V, μ_R(F) ≤ μ_{R₁}(F) + μ_{R₂}(F) in [0, ∞], where μ_{R′} := R′.measure = θ′Hⁿ⌞M′ is the weight of an IMRep R′ = (M′, θ′, ξ′) (Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V F : Set (Euclid P)) (X X₁ X₂ : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (R R₁ R₂ : IMRep V n), IsOpen V → R.Represents X → R₁.Represents X₁ → R₂.Represents X₂ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, X ω = X₁ ω + X₂ ω) → IsClosed F → F ⊆ V → R.measure F ≤ R₁.measure F + R₂.measure F
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8(b) of the parent proof (μ_{QY}(S_G) ≤ μ_{R₃}(S_G) + μ_{R_Y}(S_G), obtained from the open-set inequality via (MR), (MT) and (COB)), stated for arbitrary integer multiplicity currents and extended from compact sets to closed sets by exhaustion; the parent applies it to the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B_G, which contains the sphere S_G. Siblings: (MR) mass_and_support; (MT) mass_triangle; (COB) compact_outer_bound.
Write μ := μ_R, μ_i := μ_{R_i} (i = 1, 2) and ν := μ₁ + μ₂.
1. (Open sets.) Let G ⊆ ℝ^P be open. By (MR)(i) (V is open), μ(G) = M_G(X), μ₁(G) = M_G(X₁) and μ₂(G) = M_G(X₂). By (MT) with c := 1 (|c| ≤ 1, and X(ω) = X₁(ω) + 1·X₂(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V), in particular for those with tsupport ω ⊆ G), M_G(X) ≤ M_G(X₁) + M_G(X₂). Hence μ(G) ≤ μ₁(G) + μ₂(G) = ν(G).
2. (ν is finite on compact subsets of V.) Let K ⊆ V be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so for an IMRep R′ = (M′, θ′, ξ′) in V, μ_{R′}(K) = ∫_K θ′ d(Hⁿ⌞M′) = ∫_{M′∩K} θ′ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), which is finite by the local integrability field of R′ (K compact, K ⊆ V). So ν(K) = μ₁(K) + μ₂(K) < ∞.
3. (Compact sets.) Let K ⊆ V be compact. By step 1, μ(G) ≤ ν(G) + 0 for every open G ⊇ K, in particular for every such G with G ⊂⊂ V. By (COB) with U := V, E := K, the measures μ and ν (finite on compact subsets of V by step 2) and c := 0: μ(K) ≤ ν(K).
4. (Closed sets.) Let F ⊆ V be closed, and put F_j := F ∩ closedBall(0, j) for j ∈ ℕ. Each F_j is closed and bounded, hence compact, and F_j ⊆ F ⊆ V; the F_j increase with j, and ⋃_j F_j = F (every x lies in closedBall(0, j) for any integer j ≥ |x|). By continuity of measures from below along an increasing sequence of sets (Mathlib Monotone.measure_iUnion), step 3 and monotonicity of ν: μ(F) = sup_j μ(F_j) ≤ sup_j ν(F_j) ≤ ν(F) = μ₁(F) + μ₂(F). ∎
proof_key_steps: For open G: μ_R(G) = M_G(X) ≤ M_G(X₁) + M_G(X₂) = μ_{R₁}(G) + μ_{R₂}(G), by (MR)(i) and (MT) with c = 1.
μ_{R₁} + μ_{R₂} is finite on compact subsets of V (local integrability of the multiplicities).
(COB) with c = 0 passes the inequality to compact K ⊆ V.
A closed F ⊆ V is the increasing union of the compact sets F ∩ closedBall(0, j); continuity from below gives μ_R(F) ≤ μ_{R₁}(F) + μ_{R₂}(F).

audit.reason: The open-set inequality follows from mass_and_support and mass_triangle. Local finiteness permits compact_outer_bound on compact subsets of V; increasing compact exhaustion proves the exact closed-set conclusion without additional regularity assumptions.

subproblem.title: Additivity of a push-forward map that is linear on integer multiplicity currents with compact supports in O (step 4 of the parent)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P any set, and push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) any map (𝒟_n(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ n) such that push(X₁ − X₂) = push X₁ − push X₂ for all integer multiplicity X₁, X₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity) whose supports spt X₁, spt X₂ (GeometricCurrentOn.support, Simon 6.2.11) are compact and contained in O; here − is the contract's difference of currents, (X₁ − X₂)(ω) = X₁(ω) − X₂(ω). Let X, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with spt X and spt Y compact and contained in O. Then there is an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that S(ω) = X(ω) + Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), spt S ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, spt S is compact, and push S(ω) = push X(ω) + push Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (push : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ X₁ X₂ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity X₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity X₂ → IsCompact X₁.support → X₁.support ⊆ O → IsCompact X₂.support → X₂.support ⊆ O → push (X₁ - X₂) = push X₁ - push X₂) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y → IsCompact X.support → X.support ⊆ O → IsCompact Y.support → Y.support ⊆ O → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, S ω = X ω + Y ω) ∧ S.support ⊆ X.support ∪ Y.support ∧ IsCompact S.support ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, push S ω = push X ω + push Y ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (the current QY = Q + Y, its support, and push(Q + Y) = push Q + push Y obtained from (PF)(B)), for arbitrary X, Y in place of Q, Y. Two simplifications of the parent's argument: the support bound spt S ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y is proved directly from the definition of the zero region (instead of (p2)), and push S is computed from S − Y = X, so push 0 = 0 is not needed. Sibling: (IMC) im_calculus, part (c).
Recall that spt D = ℝ^P ∖ Z_D for D ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), where Z_D is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure(W) compact on which D vanishes (D(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport η ⊆ W); Z_D is open, so spt D is closed. Currents are determined by their values on test forms (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
1. (S and its values.) By (IMC)(c) in the open set ℝ^P, the difference of two integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P is integer multiplicity. Applying it three times, N := X − X, N − Y and S := X − (N − Y) are integer multiplicity. For every ω, N(ω) = X(ω) − X(ω) = 0, hence S(ω) = X(ω) − (0 − Y(ω)) = X(ω) + Y(ω).
2. (spt S ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y.) Let x ∉ spt X ∪ spt Y. Then x ∈ Z_X ∩ Z_Y: there are open sets W₁, W₂ containing x, with compact closures, such that X vanishes on W₁ and Y vanishes on W₂. W := W₁ ∩ W₂ is open and contains x, and closure(W) ⊆ closure(W₁) is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact. If tsupport η ⊆ W, then S(η) = X(η) + Y(η) = 0 + 0 = 0. So S vanishes on W, x ∈ Z_S, and x ∉ spt S.
3. (Compactness.) spt S is closed and, by step 2, contained in the compact set spt X ∪ spt Y; hence spt S is compact. Moreover spt S ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y ⊆ O.
4. (Additivity.) For every ω, (S − Y)(ω) = X(ω) + Y(ω) − Y(ω) = X(ω); hence S − Y = X. S and Y are integer multiplicity with compact supports contained in O (steps 1 and 3 and the hypotheses), so the hypothesis on push gives push X = push(S − Y) = push S − push Y. Evaluating at ω: push X(ω) = push S(ω) − push Y(ω), i.e. push S(ω) = push X(ω) + push Y(ω). ∎
proof_key_steps: S := X − ((X − X) − Y) is integer multiplicity by three applications of (IMC)(c), and S(ω) = X(ω) + Y(ω).
A point of Z_X ∩ Z_Y has the open neighbourhood W₁ ∩ W₂, with compact closure, on which S vanishes; so spt S ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, and spt S, being closed, is compact and contained in O.
S − Y = X, so the hypothesis on push gives push X = push S − push Y, i.e. push S = push X + push Y.

audit.reason: The difference construction supplies integer multiplicity and the sum evaluation. Intersecting zero-region neighbourhoods proves the support bound and compactness. Applying difference preservation to S and Y after verifying admissibility proves push additivity; O need not be open.

subproblem.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to a relatively compact Borel set, as a current in ℝ^P, with the complementary piece (steps 2 and 6 of the parent)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n) with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); write μ := μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure). Let E ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and K ⊆ ℝ^P compact with E ⊆ K ⊆ U. Then there exist a current Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with an IMRep R_Q in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing Q, and a current T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with an IMRep R₁ in U representing T₁, such that: (1) μ_{R_Q} = μ⌞E; (2) μ_{R₁} = μ⌞(ℝ^P ∖ E); (3) T(ω) = Q(ω) + T₁(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Q is evaluated at ω regarded as a test form on ℝ^P (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω, the same form); (4) Q(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ E (same convention); (5) spt Q ⊆ closure(E) ∩ spt T; (6) spt Q is compact. Here spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support: the domain minus the union of all open sets W with closure(W) compact and contained in the domain on which the current vanishes).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U E K : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → MeasurableSet E → IsCompact K → E ⊆ K → K ⊆ U → ∃ (Q : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (RQ : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R₁ : IMRep U n), RQ.Represents Q ∧ RQ.measure = R.measure.restrict E ∧ R₁.Represents T₁ ∧ R₁.measure = R.measure.restrict Eᶜ ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = Q (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω) + T₁ ω) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ E → Q (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) n ω) = T ω) ∧ Q.support ⊆ closure E ∩ T.support ∧ IsCompact Q.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 6 of the parent proof (the current Q = T⌞B_G transported to ℝ^P, its properties (Q1) and (Q3), and the splitting T = Q + T₁ with T₁ = T⌞(ℝ^P ∖ B_G)), stated for a Borel set E contained in a compact K ⊆ U in place of B_G ⊆ B̄_G. Simon Ch. 6, 3.1–3.2 and 2.11. Siblings: (MR) mass_and_support; (IMC) im_calculus, parts (b) and (d); (IR) imrep_restriction.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For an IMRep R′ (in any domain) with carrier M′, multiplicity θ′ and orientation ξ′, μ_{R′} := R′.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M′).withDensity θ′ and R′.action(ω) := ∫_{M′} θ′(x) ξ′(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x); both depend only on (M′, θ′, ξ′), not on the domain. For an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ write f_ω(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) = ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩. A test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is regarded as the same form in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (testFormOnInclusion; the underlying form is unchanged).
1. (Restricted triples in U.) By (IMC)(b) applied in U to R and the Borel set E, there are A₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R′ in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ (R′ represents A₁; A₁ is not used further). By (IMC)(b) applied to R and the Borel set ℝ^P ∖ E, there are T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R₁ in U with carrier M ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ E), multiplicity θ and orientation ξ, with R₁ representing T₁. By (IR)(c) for R′ (Borel set E) and for R₁ (Borel set ℝ^P ∖ E): μ_{R′} = μ⌞E and μ_{R₁} = μ⌞(ℝ^P ∖ E) — the latter is (2) — and, for every n-form ω, R′.action(ω) = ∫_E f_ω dμ and R₁.action(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P∖E} f_ω dμ. By (IR)(c) for R itself and the Borel set ℝ^P (R has carrier M = M ∩ ℝ^P, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ), R.action(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P} f_ω dμ = ∫ f_ω dμ.
2. (Transport to ℝ^P.) The triple R₂ := (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in ℝ^P. Every field of IMRep other than 'carrier ⊆ domain' and local integrability concerns only the carrier, the multiplicity and the orientation, so it is inherited from R′: M ∩ E is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ is measurable and positive on M ∩ E, ξ is Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)-a.e. strongly measurable, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E, ξ(x) orients an approximate tangent space of M ∩ E at x. The carrier lies in ℝ^P. Local integrability: if K′ ⊆ ℝ^P is compact, then (M ∩ E) ∩ K′ ⊆ M ∩ K because E ⊆ K, so ∫_{(M∩E)∩K′} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by monotonicity of the lower integral in the set (lintegral_mono_set) and the local integrability of R on the compact set K ⊆ U. Now apply (IMC)(b) in the open set ℝ^P to R₂ and the Borel set ℝ^P: there are Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R_Q in ℝ^P with carrier (M ∩ E) ∩ ℝ^P = M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ, with R_Q representing Q. Since R_Q and R′ have the same carrier, multiplicity and orientation, μ_{R_Q} = μ_{R′} = μ⌞E — this is (1) — and R_Q.action = R′.action. Hence, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) regarded in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), Q(ω) = R_Q.action(ω) = R′.action(ω) = ∫_E f_ω dμ.
3. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The form ω is smooth, hence continuous; C := tsupport ω is compact and C ⊆ U. (a) ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by (IR)(b), ω is continuous, and the evaluation pairing (L, α) ↦ L(α) on Λₙ × Λⁿ is continuous (a bounded bilinear map, isBoundedBilinearMap_apply); hence f_ω is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk, Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). (b) By (IMC)(d), for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm); since μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M by (IR)(a), this holds for μ-a.e. x. The map α ↦ |α| is continuous (the square root of a finite sum of squares of the evaluations α(e_I), each continuous in α, continuous_eval_const) and |0| = 0, so x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left) and hence bounded by a constant c (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Thus |f_ω| ≤ c μ-a.e. (c) C is closed, hence Borel, and μ(C) = ∫_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, and local integrability of R; C compact, C ⊆ U). By (a)–(c), f_ω is μ-integrable on C (an a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded function on a set of finite measure, Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). Finally f_ω vanishes outside C (there ω(x) = 0 and ξ(x) is linear), so f_ω is μ-integrable on ℝ^P (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset).
4. (Proof of (3).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Since R represents T, by step 1, by additivity of the Bochner integral over the Borel partition ℝ^P = E ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ E) for the integrable f_ω (step 3; integral_add_compl), by step 2, and since R₁ represents T₁: T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ f_ω dμ = ∫_E f_ω dμ + ∫_{ℝ^P∖E} f_ω dμ = Q(ω) + R₁.action(ω) = Q(ω) + T₁(ω).
5. (Proof of (4).) If moreover tsupport ω ⊆ E, then every x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ E lies outside tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and f_ω(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. Hence T₁(ω) = R₁.action(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P∖E} f_ω dμ = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero), and Q(ω) = T(ω) by (3).
6. (Proof of (5).) By (MR)(ii) applied to Q in the open set ℝ^P with the representation R_Q, spt Q = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_{R_Q} = spt(μ⌞E). For every measure μ and every set E, spt(μ⌞E) ⊆ closure(E) ∩ spt μ (Mathlib Measure.support_restrict_subset): a point outside closure(E) has the open neighbourhood ℝ^P ∖ closure(E), which is μ⌞E-null, and μ⌞E ≤ μ. Since K is compact, hence closed, and E ⊆ K, closure(E) ⊆ K ⊆ U. By (MR)(ii) applied to T in U with R, spt T = U ∩ spt μ. Hence every x ∈ spt Q satisfies x ∈ closure(E), x ∈ U and x ∈ spt μ, i.e. x ∈ closure(E) ∩ spt T.
7. (Proof of (6).) spt Q = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_{R_Q} is closed (the support of a measure is closed, Measure.isClosed_support), and by step 6 it is contained in closure(E) ⊆ K, a compact set. A closed subset of a compact set is compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: (IMC)(b) in U gives IMReps R′ = (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) and R₁ = (M ∖ E, θ, ξ), R₁ representing T₁; (IR)(c) gives μ_{R′} = μ⌞E, μ_{R₁} = μ⌞(ℝ^P ∖ E), the actions ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ and ∫_{ℝ^P∖E} ξ(ω) dμ, and R.action(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ.
(M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in ℝ^P (local integrability from E ⊆ K with K compact in U); (IMC)(b) in ℝ^P yields Q represented by R_Q with μ_{R_Q} = μ⌞E and Q(ω) = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ.
For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ξ(ω) is μ-integrable: a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded by sup|ω| via (IMC)(d) and μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, and supported in tsupport ω, which has finite μ-measure.
T(ω) = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ + ∫_{ℝ^P∖E} ξ(ω) dμ = Q(ω) + T₁(ω); if tsupport ω ⊆ E the second integral vanishes, so Q(ω) = T(ω).
(MR)(ii): spt Q = spt(μ⌞E) ⊆ closure(E) ∩ spt μ and spt T = U ∩ spt μ with closure(E) ⊆ K ⊆ U; spt Q is closed inside the compact K, hence compact.

audit.reason: All witnesses and conclusions match the prose. The fixed compact K supplies ambient local integrability; the proved integrability justifies splitting the action. The support-restriction lemma and closure(E) ⊆ K ⊆ U establish the support and compactness conclusions using precisely the declared dependencies.
